TITLE: Internal Status Update: Project Nolaor and Project Soramis

Project Nolaor, which carries the audit finding ID XC-1856-X, continues to be a critical focus within the organization. The project is staffed by 30 people, drawn from various internal functions including finance, procurement, and compliance. The team has been working closely to address the audit findings related to internal control gaps and documentation inconsistencies. Recent work has included the development of new procedures and the reinforcement of existing processes to align with updated internal audit requirements.

Project Soramis is progressing according to plan and is on track for its target completion in Q3 FY26. The project has successfully moved past the initial resource planning stage and is now entering the execution phase. Cross-functional collaboration has improved, and stakeholder engagement remains strong, particularly in the areas of operations and strategy. The overall objective of Project Soramis is to enhance supply chain performance, and recent modeling efforts have demonstrated that the proposed interventions are likely to support long-term cost optimization goals.

Liluan Nemlurel is leading the development of demand forecasting models within Project Soramis. Her work has been instrumental in identifying key seasonal trends, which has informed more precise inventory planning. Liluan is also collaborating with the finance lead to integrate the latest model outputs into the Q3 FY26 budgeting process, ensuring that strategic assumptions are reflected in financial planning.

Risk management remains a priority for both projects. In the case of Project Nolaor, the team is monitoring the availability of compliance subject matter experts. This shortage could affect the timeline for completing the final audit response deliverables. To mitigate this risk, the project team has initiated discussions with the compliance department to secure additional support and has arranged for a coordination meeting with the finance team to review potential budget implications.

For Project Soramis, the primary risk is the possibility of delays in the delivery of custom software tools from the current vendor. While the project is currently on schedule, the team is developing contingency measures to account for any unforeseen disruptions. The project lead has begun reaching out to alternative vendors to evaluate other options and maintain project flexibility.

Looking forward, the next key action for Project Nolaor is the organization of a workshop to finalize the audit response framework. This session is scheduled for the end of the quarter and will include participation from the compliance and operations teams to ensure that the response meets the expectations of the internal audit function.

For Project Soramis, the next major milestone is the completion of the pilot phase, expected to occur in mid-Q3 FY26. The team will begin preparing for this phase in the coming weeks, including the drafting of testing protocols and the securing of stakeholder approvals.

Liluan Nemlurel will continue to advance the forecasting models and will present updated findings during the next budget review. Her team is also finalizing a technical overview for internal stakeholders, which will be shared for feedback and refinement.

Both initiatives are progressing steadily, with teams remaining focused on meeting objectives and managing risks. Continued coordination across departments and vigilance regarding potential challenges will be key to maintaining this positive trajectory.
